small_guidance:
- The GEMM (32768×1024 × 1024×4096) dominates the 7.19 ms runtime; tuning the fused swish+GN kernel further yields little. Try `num_warps=4` for BLOCK_C=64 and ensure the GN reduction uses `tl.sum(y_f, axis=0)` directly (no mask needed since C=64 is power of 2 — drop BLOCK_C padding entirely).
- Fuse the swish+bias epilogue into a custom Triton GEMM rather than calling `addmm` then a separate kernel; saves one full read/write of the 32768×4096 fp32 tensor (~512 MB traffic).
- For the GN-only path (if keeping addmm), use `BLOCK_C = C = 64` exactly, `num_warps=2`, `num_stages=2`, and load gamma/beta once per group (constant across rows) — but row-parallelism makes this minor.
large_guidance:
- Replace `torch.addmm` with a custom tiled Triton GEMM (BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=32, GROUP_M=8, num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4) that fuses linear-bias + swish + bias-add directly in the accumulator epilogue, writing the post-swish-post-bias tensor. This is where the bulk of the 7 ms lives.
- Then run the GroupNorm kernel as today (one program per (row, group), C=64 channels per group fits easily in registers). Optionally fuse GN into the GEMM epilogue only if BLOCK_N is sized to a multiple of C and one group fits per N-tile — otherwise keep GN as a second small kernel.
- Consider tf32 / fp16 accumulation paths on the GEMM if accuracy budget (5e-2) allows; on RTX 4090 Ada tensor cores this can ~2× the matmul throughput. Keep the GN in fp32 for stability.
